text:
ria: RFC follow-up: propose a "local-governor" pattern for Dedicated pools. control-plane issues budgets, operator enforces local token-buckets and can act fast.
noah: Sounds promising. Main question: what controls preempt behavior when local tokens exhausted?
taylor: Idea: two-tier tokens: long_budget (control-plane) and burst_tokens (operator-local). Operator can consume burst_tokens up to X, but must decrement long_budget via a ledger call when steady-state is reached.
asha: We should also avoid split-brain during network partitions. Operator must have a small autonomous policy with sensible defaults.
ria: Sketch of ledger call: POST /v1/pool-ledger/update { pool, shard, delta_long_budget, intent_id, ttl_seconds } control-plane sends intents with monotonic intent_id. operator only applies if intent_id >= last_seen.
noah: Good. Add a smoothing rule: operator ramps prewarm by no more than 20% of current prewarm per 30s window (configurable). prevents oscillation.
taylor: EWMA smoothing works too, with alpha configurable. Also need circuit-breaker: if control-plane unreachable for > 2m, operator switches to fallback_policy: reserve_percent for critical_tenants, clamp burst_tokens to low watermark.
asha: We need a minimal proto or JSON schema for intents so other teams can integrate.
ria: Example intent JSON: ```json { "pool_id": "dedicated-us-west-1-a", "intent_id": 2025041201, "desired_headroom_slots": 6, "max_burst_tokens": 40, "reserved_for_critical_pct": 12, "ttl_seconds": 90 } ```
noah: Metrics contract: operator must emit these metrics with labels (pool, shard, region, tenant): dedicated_pool_headroom_slots, dedicated_pool_burst_tokens, dedicated_pool_intent_id_last_seen, dedicated_pool_fallback_mode{0|1}.
taylor: Also trace events for preempt actions: preempt.event with fields (from_tenant,to_tenant,reason,intent_id). Keep them small but searchable.
asha: CRD fields suggestion for operator config: spec.operator.allowed_burst_pct, spec.operator.ramp_pct_per_window, spec.operator.fallback.reserve_pct, spec.operator.intent_ttl_seconds. We can gate rollout via feature-flag on the control-plane side.
ria: Failure-mode notes: 1) Control-plane sends aggressive headroom reduction -> operator should back off with a grace window and emit an alert so SRE can inspect. 2) Operator miscounts tokens due to clock skew -> use monotonic counters and idempotent ledger updates.
noah: Test plan: deterministic sim with 100 tenants, spike patterns, partition control-plane for 5-10 minutes, measure preempt churn, latency SLO violations, and fairness delta. Put results in repo under infra-sims.
taylor: Action items: ria -> draft intent api + sample client; noah -> metric + alerting dashboard; asha -> CRD + operator fallback impl; ops-bot: scheduled smoke-runner on staging nightly.
ops-bot: Nightly job scheduled: dedicated-pool-sim -> staging (start 02:00 UTC).
ria: Thanks. If no blockers Ill fold this into the RFC follow-up doc and open PRs tomorrow.
noah: No blockers from security/eng infra perspective.
taylor: Fine by me, prefer alpha rollout to a single region first.
asha: +1, will create tests to validate idempotent ledger writes.
ria: Great, pulling this into the RFC.
